01

Data controller and contact details

The controller of personal data is Viacheslav Uspenskyi, the developer of Juno (“we”).

For questions about data processing, contact support@junoreads.com. Further details are available in the Support section.

02

Our legal bases for processing data

  • Operating Juno and Premium — performing the agreement covering use of the app and purchased access. We process only the data needed for the functions you request.
  • Support — performing that agreement when assistance relates to its performance; for other enquiries, our legitimate interest in answering your question.
  • Diagnostics and security — our legitimate interest in identifying faults and protecting Juno against abuse, using necessary technical data, including IP addresses to limit request rates.
  • Legal matters — complying with specific legal obligations, including handling data requests; our legitimate interest in protecting our rights in a dispute.

We rely on legitimate interests where they are not overridden by the need to protect your fundamental rights and freedoms. You may submit a reasoned objection.

Using Juno, reading this policy or sending an email does not, by itself, constitute consent to any processing. Where consent is required, we request it separately and explain how to withdraw it.

These are the bases for our processing. Providers’ processing for their own purposes is explained in their policies linked below.

03

Learning data on your device

Juno stores learning progress, reading and listening positions, bookmarks, learned words, exercise states, earned rewards and settings on your device. This allows you to continue learning.

The current version does not send this learning data to the developer’s server and does not provide its own cloud synchronisation of progress. Downloaded materials and audio may also be stored on your device for reuse.

You do not need to create a separate Juno account or give us your name, telephone number or email address to learn.

04

Downloading materials and technical data

The materials for the two free books, “Little Red-Cap” and “Lazy Jack”, are included in the app. Juno uses Cloudflare Workers and R2 storage to deliver server-hosted Premium materials and audio.

When a request is made, the infrastructure receives the IP address, technical connection headers, resource address and request parameters, including book, chapter or audio identifiers. Our code uses the IP address to limit the rate of access-verification requests. Purchase verification data is processed as described in Premium purchases.

After verifying access, the server issues temporary links to materials. Requesting a material does not necessarily mean it has been read or listened to: audio may be downloaded in advance for offline learning.

Storage of our Worker’s request and execution logs is disabled. This does not mean that Cloudflare performs no processing: the provider processes network data to operate and protect its infrastructure. Its own processing is described in the Cloudflare policy; retention is covered under Retention and deletion.

How we protect data

The app’s connections to our API and the transfer of materials are protected by HTTPS, which encrypts data in transit. The server verifies Apple’s signature and Premium entitlement, issues short-lived authorisations and links, and limits the rate of access-verification requests.

We minimise server-side data: we do not send learning progress to the server, do not maintain a permanent database of purchase verification records, and have disabled storage of our Worker’s logs. We verify the requester’s identity before providing personal data in response to a request.

Processing locations and provider terms

EU jurisdiction is configured for the R2 storage of learning files. This restriction applies to R2 object storage, not to all Workers request processing or Cloudflare service data. The provider has global infrastructure; data may be processed in the United States, the EEA and other countries.

Cloudflare provides a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) incorporated into its standard service terms. It sets out Cloudflare’s obligations when processing personal data on the customer’s behalf within its scope. The DPA provides for processing according to customer instructions, data protection, assistance with exercising rights, and return or deletion of data when services end, subject to exceptions required by law. Cloudflare also publishes a list of subprocessors.

More about file locations: R2 jurisdictions.

05

Premium purchases

Apple processes Premium payments through the App Store. Juno receives technical purchase information through StoreKit to unlock Premium, restore purchases and account for revoked access rights.

To obtain server-hosted materials, the app sends Apple-signed proof of purchase to our API on Cloudflare. This includes app, product, transaction and original transaction identifiers, dates and purchase status information. The server verifies the signature and contacts Apple for current transaction information. After successful verification, it issues a short-lived authorisation to obtain materials.

Our code does not create a permanent server-side database of purchase verification records or transaction history. This does not eliminate processing during verification or Apple’s and Cloudflare’s own policies. We do not receive your bank card number, its security code or your Apple Account password.

Apple’s data processing is described in Apple’s Privacy Policy.

06

Support correspondence

When you email support@junoreads.com, we receive your email address, the sender’s name if provided, the message and any attachments. We use these to respond and resolve your enquiry.

Email is provided by Infomaniak Network SA, which receives, stores and sends messages. For this processing, we are the data controller and Infomaniak is the processor, processing correspondence on our behalf under a concluded data processing agreement (DPA).

The agreement provides for processing according to our instructions to deliver the services, security measures, confidentiality and restrictions on staff access, and assistance in handling personal data requests. Information about protecting hosted data is available on Infomaniak’s data protection page.

Separately, Infomaniak may process data as an independent controller for its own purposes, as described in its Privacy Policy. That processing is not covered by our agreement for processing on the customer’s behalf.

Do not send passwords, full bank card details, documents or other information that is not needed to handle your enquiry.

07

Support and privacy website

When you visit this website hosted on GitHub Pages, GitHub stores visitors’ IP addresses for security, even when they are not signed in, as described in the Pages documentation. GitHub acts as an independent data controller for its own purposes.

This website contains no advertising scripts, analytics, forms or cookies of our own. The contact link opens your email app; you choose whether to send the email.

GitHub may process data in the United States and other countries. Transfer conditions and safeguards are described in its Privacy Statement. Retention periods depend on the purpose, legal obligations and disputes; GitHub does not specify a separate exact retention period for Pages visitors’ IP addresses.

For GitHub’s own processing, contact privacy@github.com; for ours, contact Juno support. Our email deletion periods do not apply to GitHub logs.

08

Advertising and permissions

The current version of Juno contains no advertising SDKs or third-party behavioural analytics systems. We do not sell personal data or use it to track you across apps and websites for advertising purposes.

Juno does not request access to your contacts, camera, microphone or precise location.

09

Retention and deletion

On your device

Learning data is retained so you can continue your activities. Deleting Juno together with its data removes the local copy; system backups depend on your operating system settings. Apple’s purchase history remains, and payment is not automatically refunded.

After a confirmed loss of Premium, bookmarks from paid books return to the Backpack and those books’ unfinished activities are reset: mode completion, audio position, viewed words, and training and exercise states. Text position, completed chapters, rewards, words in the Notebook and progress in free books are retained. A purchase-verification error does not trigger a reset.

Cloudflare server-side processing

Our code processes proof of purchase when verifying a request, without writing it to a permanent database. Access authorisation is valid for 5 minutes and a file link for 15 minutes. These are access validity periods, not deletion periods for all provider data. R2 stores learning materials, not users’ progress or a database of their purchases.

Disabling Worker log storage does not set a deletion period for Cloudflare service data. For its own processing, the provider determines retention according to the purpose, nature of the data and legal obligations, as stated in section 11 of its policy.

Support correspondence

We retain ordinary emails and attachments for as long as they are needed to handle the enquiry. Once the issue is finally resolved and the enquiry is closed, we delete them from our mailbox and delete copies we have saved.

For a specific dispute or legal requirement, we retain only the necessary material until the need ends or the required period expires, and then delete it. Deletion from the mailbox does not mean simultaneous deletion from Infomaniak backups and system logs; see the provider’s guidance.

Records of enquiries and data operations

Working records of enquiries (reference number, dates, status and outcome) follow the same deletion rules as correspondence.

For records of personal data operations — date and time, action, person performing it, purpose and basis — paragraph 3.11 of the Model Procedure provides for retention until the end of the calendar year following the year of the operation, unless the law provides otherwise. Email contents and attachments are not included in these records; their retention period is not extended.

10

Your rights and requests

Under Article 8 of the Law of Ukraine “On Personal Data Protection”, you have the right to:

  • know the sources, storage location and purpose of processing, the controllers and processors and their locations, recipients and conditions of access;
  • obtain confirmation of processing and access to your data;
  • submit a reasoned objection and, if data is inaccurate or unlawfully processed, request its correction or destruction;
  • where processing is based on consent, specify restrictions when giving consent and withdraw it;
  • know how automated processing works and be protected against automated decisions with legal consequences;
  • be protected against unlawful processing, loss or damage to data and use legal remedies.

This summary does not limit the full range of rights under the law, including additional rights granted by other applicable legislation.

How to make a request

Email support@junoreads.com, specifying the data concerned and what you would like us to do. You can request deletion of correspondence at any time. A legal representative may also submit a request. Before granting access to data, we verify the requester’s identity and the representative’s authority. Do not send copies of documents without prior agreement.

We cannot remotely access progress on your device. For its deletion and retention periods for other data, see Retention and deletion.

Response times

For access requests, we communicate our decision or the legal grounds for refusal within 10 working days of receipt. We provide the data no later than 30 calendar days after receipt, except where the law provides otherwise.

We consider a reasoned objection or a request to change or destroy inaccurate or unlawfully processed data within 10 days of receipt.

Any refusal is based on the law; a provider’s technical limitations do not remove your rights.

Where to complain

You may complain to the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights or to a court, without being required to contact us first.

11

Changes to this policy

We will update this policy if Juno’s features, data processing practices or applicable requirements change. The current version will show its last updated date.
